summary: Dashboards, reports, charts, sharing and tools as SwiftUI screens.

src/charts/BarList.jsx.note: A Grid of label (136, or 200 for NSIDs set a step smaller), bar (at least 96, or 60) and value, at most 640 wide; each row read as its title or label and its value. The web's label may be markup; here a row says whether its label is an NSID (`code`).

src/charts/ChartTable.jsx.note: ChartTable and ShowAsTable: the line under a chart (Show as table as a link action, then the chart's other actions), and the buckets newest first in a DataTable of at most 320 points that scrolls inside, with the trend's column named as the legend names it.

src/charts/Heatmap.jsx.note: A Grid of the day labels and the cells on the --heat ramp (ChartFormat.heatSteps), empty cells outlined and the best ringed, the hours under them over their spans, and the legend; the summary is the grid's VoiceOver label, each cell's title its tooltip (.help).

src/charts/SeriesChart.jsx.note: In Swift Charts over bucket indices (equal slots): bars (at most 24 wide, a 2-point gap, 90% with the pressed one whole) or a line over the wash with its last dot; the trend (broken at gaps) and its legend; the second line, dashed, or stacked with its wash; the ghost's dashed reach past the last bucket with its open dot and words (drawn through the chart's proxy); the marks' rules and diamonds, and the newest five listed under the chart; the rules with their numbers (fmtTick) and the dates under the first, middle and last bucket (axisStops); a press is the hover (chartXSelection), with the crosshair, the markers and the readout on its own ground; the web's aria label. Swift Charts lays out the plot's margins and the rules' numbers itself (on the leading axis rather than on each rule at the column's edge), and a bar's foot is rounded as well as its top.

src/charts/Sparkline.jsx.note: The web's 100 by 30 box stretched to the width given, 32 tall, the line 1.5 over the wash; hidden from VoiceOver.

src/dashboards/DashboardPage.jsx.note: The header (the name with its ⋯: Rename, Duplicate, New dashboard, Reset or Clear with its toast, Delete with its dialog; the period's line; Customize and the period picker; Done), the twelve-column grid with dashboards.css's narrowing (CardGrid), the cards under their titles with the way to the full report, the empty state, ?edit=1, and Customize as the web's phone and keyboard path at every width (each card a line to move up or down, its size, Remove, with toasts) with the library in a dialog (search, kind, Add). The card settings dialog (title, period, kind of engagement, rows, Use the defaults) opens from a card's line in Customize. OwnLine says a card's own period and kind under its title, and Post this chart is each chart card's PostChartButton (the share dialog). Not yet, and why: dragging cards and reports; SwiftUI's draggable and dropDestination give no place between two cards of a custom twelve-column layout to drop on, and List's onMove, the system's long-press reorder, can't hold the grid; the up and down controls are the whole web keyboard path, and VoiceOver's. Nor the chosen card's floating tools.

src/dashboards/DashboardsContext.jsx.note: ShellDashboards is the provider: the layout read once per account under virga:dashboards:<did> through Layouts.sanitizeLayout (the three starting dashboards when nothing is stored), and every action (add, duplicate, rename, delete, move and reset a dashboard, reset all, add, remove, resize and move a card, a card's options) applied with VirgaInsights' Layouts and written back at once as DashboardLayout's JSON; a refused write keeps the change for the run. The web's replaceDashboard has no caller here yet.

src/dashboards/NewDashboardDialog.jsx.note: The name (at most 60) and Start from (Empty, or a template with its count), Create; an empty dashboard opens for customizing (?edit=1).

src/dashboards/widgets/content.jsx.note: A typical post, media described, formats (with its standout sentence) and length, tags and sites, each with its foot and the line for an archive the next sync must read first.

src/dashboards/widgets/index.jsx.note: Every card: the figures (followers, new followers, unfollows, engagement, per post, given, posts, blocked by), the charts (follower growth with the ghost and the milestones, new followers, engagement over time, rate, by type and given, posting cadence, Best time, blocks over time, repo activity) with the notes marked, and the lists (top posts, top engagers, you engage with, follow-back, newest followers, unfollows, the lists you're on, records by collection) with Follow and the names filled in. WIDGET_HEADS: the follower chart's Total and New in its heading, and the lists' count under the title of the lists you're on.

src/dashboards/widgets/parts.jsx.note: ROWS and HEIGHT (WidgetParts), and Stat: the label (a link to its report) with its glyph, the window, the number at --figure-size, the trend beside it on a card wider than a quarter, and the note line in parts.

src/dashboards/widgets/posting.jsx.note: Its cards (scheduled, timers, going out next, latest drafts) are in the library and on the grid with their titles, and say they need the composer, which isn't in the app yet.

src/people/people.jsx.note: cardFor, displayName and profileUrl (People), and PersonRow: the picture, the name (a link to the profile), the handle where the name isn't it, follows you, a fact, the value, Follow (archive.setFollow, held while the sync reads follows, its error under the name) and the way to the Interaction lookup. useWantActors is a .task on the rows shown. Not yet: a row followed under Not following stays until the filter changes on the web (useFollow's kept set); here it leaves at once. FollowButton is the kit's small button.

src/reports/ChartNotes.jsx.note: Notes on your charts: the day (the system's date picker, up to today) and what happened (at most 80), Add note, the notes newest first with Remove, and the empty line, over one AnnotationsModel per account (ChartNotesModels); on the followers, posts and engagement reports. useChartMarks is ChartNotesModels.marks: the notes, and the follower milestones on the follower charts, on the reports' charts and the dashboard's. The widget's visually hidden marks list (.widget .an-chart-marks) is drawn under the card's chart here.

src/reports/ContentReport.jsx.note: The figures, by format and by length (each with its standout sentence, typical post or posts, and its table), tags and sites (the first twelve, Show all, their table), threads, languages (named in English by the system's Locale, as Intl.DisplayNames(['en']) does), the line on posts not read, the two SyncEmpty states and How this is counted, word for word.

src/reports/PostRow.jsx.note: PostRowView with postText, postUrl and postWhen: the words (a link to the post on Bluesky), when (relative within a week, else the short date with the year when it isn't this one), reply and quote, and the counts by kind (the ones not counted dimmed), or the one total with its rank.

src/reports/ReportPage.jsx.note: ReportsIndex and every report: Followers (Total, With blocks, per bucket; the unfollow figure; newest followers; biggest days with the post that day or the day before; How this is counted), Posts, Engagement (received or given, by kind; top posts), Content, Blocks, People (by kind; everyone, not following or following) and Atmosphere, each chart with its table and notes. Add to dashboard (REPORT_WIDGET, AddToDashboard) is a link action in the header beside the period picker, where the web puts it on the line under the chart (and in a phone's ⋯); the new-dashboard toast has no Open it link (a toast here holds words only).

src/reports/parts.jsx.note: Card (ReportCard), ModeToggle (a small Segmented, each key's title its VoiceOver name), unitOptions, fig, SyncEmpty (with Sync now), HowCounted (a Disclosure) and GroupTable (a bar list's table behind Show as table).

src/share/ShareDialog.jsx.note: Post this chart as a sheet: the spec from ShareSpec.shareSpec over the card's type, its own settings and the account's notes (Annotations.readAnnotations), for the card's period or the page's; 'There’s nothing on this card to draw yet.'; the picture (ShareImage, the on-screen theme's colours) with its edge, 'Drawing the picture…' or the failure; the description (ShareSpec.shareAltText) in a text area held to 2,000 with its hint, over the limit past 1,800; Save the picture (into Photos, add-only, after asking; a toast says it was saved or couldn't be: iOS's own words, as a browser's download needs none) and Write a post with it, first and on its own line on a phone. Write a post with it opens the composer through the `shareComposer` environment hook (asDid, sharePostText, the PNG and the description) once a composer sets it; until then it is a ShareLink of virga-chart.png with the post's first line. The hook for the dashboards and reports: PostChartButton (a card's ghost icon, 'Post <name> as a picture'), PostChartLink ('Post this chart') and .shareDialog($request, period:) with ShareRequest.

src/tools/ArchiveSearch.jsx.note: matchesWords (a word in the text or the sites linked; a # word a whole tag, any case, or the written tag on an older row), the window, the kind, the sort (newest, oldest, most engagement then newest, in V8's sort) over the archive's posts; the toolbar (the search field, Kind of post, Sort), the count with what was searched for, the line until the archive's content shape, Export as a menu (these posts and every post as CSV, everything as JSON, through the system's exporter), each post as PostRow (two lines of its words, the way to it on Bluesky, its meta line of when, reply or quote, and its counts), Show 30 more and the caption. The search isn't deferred.

src/tools/BestTime.jsx.note: The header with the period picker offering 90d, 1y, All and Custom (the window in use pressed: bestTimeWindow reads the year under 90 days), the sentence (bestTimeSentence), the heatmap with Hours per column (Hourly, 2 hours, 4 hours; cells 22 or 30 tall), the caption, every slot with posts as a table under Show as table (in a 384-point window), the best slots (rank, when, typical, posts; on a phone the posts under the slot) with the way to the weekly schedule, and By weekday as a BarList with its caption, side by side from 400 a column. The zone is the device's (TimeZone identifier, underscores as spaces).

src/tools/FollowBack.jsx.note: The queue over followBackModel for the period, less the dismissed (KeepListModel 'followback' on the app's key-value store): its count and line, Bring back N dismissed, the callout before the follows are read, a person row each (the count of interactions, then kindsLine by count where the row has room; Follow back; the ✕ that dismisses), anyone followed from here kept at the top as 'followed just now' until the page is left, Show 25 more, and the caption. People rows are ToolParts' port of people.jsx's PersonRow and useFollow.

src/tools/FollowCleanup.jsx.note: Every follow once (the earliest record), with its interactions (all, and the last year), whether they follow you, and the activity on its card; the header's line; the callout before the follows are read; the activity check (ArchiveModel.checkActivity through the session's network, its progress with Stop, which cancels it, then the toast), Quiet after 30/90/180/365 days; the four filter figures; the line over the table (the sort, Show/Hide kept, Export 'follows'; or the count selected with Clear, Keep, don’t suggest and Unfollow n; or Unfollowing n of m…); the table from 641 wide (CleanupTable: the tick box with Select every account shown in the head, the account at 36% of the table's width with its name and handle ending in an ellipsis, then Follows you, Last active with its dot, Interactions and Followed sharing what is left, and Unfollow or Undo with its error; a ticked row tinted past the sides; an unfollowed row muted, its name struck through), and narrower as the web's phone sets it (Select all shown; each row's tick box, face, name, handle and Kept, its button and error, and the meta line: the activity with its dot, followed, follows you, interactions); while rows are ticked each row's own button steps back, keeping its place; Show 50 more; the caption; and the confirm dialog. The kept list is KeepListModel 'cleanup'.

src/tools/Identity.jsx.note: The account (the open account's profile: face, name, handle), the four figures (followers, following, posts, the year it was made with the day under it, from the PLC log's first operation or the profile's createdAt), Identifiers (the DID in the code face, the handle or 'Not verified right now', the PDS from Atproto.resolvePds while 'Looking it up…' or 'Couldn’t be resolved', the DID document's host as a link; Copy on each, which says Copied for a moment), the handle and server history from Atproto.getPlcHistory (historyEvents: created, handle changed, moved, deactivated, newest first, on a timeline; 'Reading the log…', a did:web's line, or the directory's), and the repo's records, collections, apps and oldest record with the way to the Atmosphere report. Both reads go through the session's transport and DID-document cache (the archive's environment).

src/tools/InteractionLookup.jsx.note: The chosen account in the address (?who= on the navigator, cleared when the page is left), an address that names a handle looked up through Atproto.getProfile on the session's transport (missing or failed in a warn callout); PersonSearch (matchPeople's seven floating over the page 6 under the field, the lookup option for a whole handle or DID, 'Looking up @…', the not-found and couldn’t-reach lines, the hint; on a hardware keyboard ↑ and ↓ open the suggestions and move through them, round at the ends, the pointer's row becoming the active one, Return taking it and Escape closing them, the active one read as the field's value); StartingPoint with its legend, PairCount and Show 12 more; Chosen: the person (Open on Bluesky, Choose someone else, the three facts), By kind, each way (bars to the largest, the sum, first and latest), Interactions per month (both ways, the line under the chart and its table, the caption), the posts they engaged with (or the line why not) and your replies and quotes, Every interaction (Direction and Kind, Export as one file or a choice, each event's date, glyph, phrase, words and its post), and How this is counted.

src/tools/ListsYoureOn.jsx.note: Before lists are read: the sentence and Sync now; none: No lists here. Then the three filter figures (Every list, Moderation lists with their subscribers, Curation lists), the count with Export ('lists'), and the lists: from 641 wide a table (ListsTable: List, the way to it on Bluesky, or Untitled list; Made by, @owner or Unknown account with the DID as its pointer's tip and its hint; Kind, Moderation a step louder; Subscribers, moderation lists only, or —; You were added, or —); narrower as the web's phone sets the row: the name with its kind at the right and a meta line of by @owner, its subscribers and when you were added, a cell with nothing to say left out (an owner whose name hasn't been read is left out, as on a phone).

src/tools/ToolPage.jsx.note: ToolHeader (Tools in the crumbs, the name, the line, what it touches, and the page's controls), the page of a tool that isn't built (or of an address that names none) with See every tool, and ToolsIndex: the kinds in two columns where there is room (each at least 360), each kind's heading over a rule in ink, a row per tool (its glyph, name, line, AccessLine with 'Not built yet.' for a planned one, and useToolStats' line: follows and checked, the last sync's unfollows, the queue, lists and moderation lists, accounts on record, posts, collections), the way in at the right; a planned tool is a quieter row that goes nowhere.

src/tools/UnfollowTracker.jsx.note: Before a second list: the sentence and Sync now. Then the four figures (the last sync's, and in all since the log began), Left and Arrived as the heading's keys with Sync now and Export (ArchiveModel.exportRows 'follower-changes', through the system's exporter) at the right, the changes under the sync that noticed each (Noticed …, since the sync on … · n), each a person row with the log's card standing in, 'had followed you since …' or 'followed …', Show 40 more, and the caption. The 'in this browser' words are the web's.
